classification.difficultyReason: Directly applies the taught warning about joining unrelated categories: explain that connecting separate people's ages suggests meaningful intermediate values.

content.prompt: Explain why a line graph is not appropriate for this data.

spec.description: Intentionally inappropriate connected family-age observations. Categories are Mum, Dad, Bill and Sister. Vertical ticks run from 0 to 50 by tens. Four horizontal and seven vertical gridlines are retained, with unlabelled baseline ticks and no arrowheads.
spec.mathematics: Dad is on 40 and Bill on 10. Mum and Sister are drawn at approximately 37 and 17 solely to reproduce the reviewed source appearance; these estimates are not exact givens. Straight segments between unrelated categories are the intended assessment defect.
spec.answerVisibility: The faulty connecting line is permanent question evidence and must remain visible. No corrective annotations are added.

answer.short: The people are separate categories; values between them have no meaning.
answer.worked: Mum, Dad, Bill and Sister are unrelated categories on the horizontal axis. Joining their ages suggests meaningful values between people, such as halfway between Bill and Sister. A column graph would compare their ages without suggesting those intermediate values.
